newsitem.title: USA: Labor's Hamel says jobs data shows strong economy.
newsitem.headline: Labor's Hamel says jobs data shows strong economy.

text.p: August's increase in job creation and drop in unemployment show the U.S. economy remains strong, Labor Department official Harvey Hamel said Friday.

Interviewed on Reuters Financial Television, Hamel, an economist at the Bureau of Labor Statistics, said data showing job creation totaling 250,000 and a cut in the jobless rate to 5.1 percent in August, in part, reflected hiring by local governments for the start of the school year as well as a return by students to their classes.
"The overall unemployment figure for August suggests that the economy is still strong," Hamel said.
He noted that private employment growth was 173,000 during August, which was "somewhat short" of the monthly gain that the country had been enjoying during this year.
"In otherwards, what I am saying is that quite a bit of the gain in August was in public employment, specifically local education," he said.
The turnaround in factory job creation, which rose by 25,000, reflected, in part, a return to work by autoworkers and their suppliers from a shutdown for re-tooling, he said.
